question:
A group of students is asked to evaluate $$I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\sin x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx$$ without finding an antiderivative of the quotient. On the interval $\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$, the denominator is positive, so the integrand is well defined. The students use the property that for an integral over $[a,b]$, replacing $x$ by $a+b-x$ produces an equivalent definite integral. In this case, the transformation interchanges the roles of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$. By comparing the original and transformed integrals, they obtain a much simpler integral and evaluate $I$ without directly integrating the original fraction.

(a) Apply the transformation $x\mapsto\frac{\pi}{2}-x$ and write an equivalent expression for $I$.

(b) Add the original and transformed expressions and simplify the resulting integrand.

(c) Evaluate $I$.

(d) If $J=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\cos x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx$, determine $J$ without further integration and justify your conclusion.
explanation:
(a)
Using the property $$\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\int_a^b f(a+b-x)\,dx$$ with $a=0$ and $b=\frac{\pi}{2}$, $$I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)+\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}\,dx$$ Since $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)=\cos x$ and $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)=\sin x$, $$I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\cos x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx$$

(b)
Adding the original and transformed forms, $$2I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{\sin x}{\sin x+\cos x}+\frac{\cos x}{\sin x+\cos x}\right)dx$$ Therefore, $$2I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}1\,dx$$

(c)
Hence, $$2I=\left[x\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}=\frac{\pi}{2}$$ Therefore, $$I=\frac{\pi}{4}$$

(d)
From part (a), the transformed form of $I$ is exactly $$J=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\cos x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx$$ Therefore, $J=I$. Hence, $$J=\frac{\pi}{4}$$ This conclusion follows from the symmetry property of definite integrals and requires no separate integration.

options.D:
(a) $I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\cos x}{\sin x-\cos x}\,dx$
(b) $2I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\sin x+\cos x}{\sin x-\cos x}\,dx$
(c) $I=0$
(d) $J=\frac{\pi}{2}$
